headline: Reference-free DockQ-style scoring compares protein interfaces across MD frames
label: Protein Interface Quality Assessment
summary: A symmetric, reference-free interface score for MD frames arrives alongside new ion channel structural analyses.
synthesis: The dominant thread is quantitative assessment of protein-protein interface geometry. MDQ adapts DockQ-style logic into a symmetric, reference-free score that compares interfaces across molecular dynamics frames and yields a distance metric for clustering conformations. Its novelty lies in computing interface similarity without a reference structure, so conformations can be compared directly from simulation output. The other two items are heterogeneous and only loosely related to this thread. A multiscale study (CG-MD, SILCS, docking) maps cholesterol-binding regions on TRPV6 across open and closed states, compared with cryo-EM sterol positions. A statistical method clusters residue-residue contact energies across aligned ion channel structures to identify folding determinants, tested on KcsA. Their outputs and data types differ from MDQ, so their results are not directly comparable to its interface metric.
